params.place: on the map: the Earth from space, then north Wales

moments.what: the globe turns, Britain lights up and is traced
a lightning pin drops on north Wales
the camera dives onto a dark mountain, a glow leaking from its side
the camera is close on the mountain, WALES writes on

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Why did Britain hide a whole power station inside a mountain in Wales?

params.place: on the map: Elidir Fawr, the mountain from above

moments.what: sheep graze on the green mountain top
the mountain's name writes on beside its peak
the park's name stamps on the map
the mountain's side tears open in rock on a lit hall, its height on a sign
a giant turbine rises in the cavern
more turbines appear in a row
the turbines spin, the cavern lights flicker

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Under the grass of Elidir Fawr, in Snowdonia, there is a cave 51 m high, with giant machines spinning in the dark.

params.place: a cut through Elidir Fawr: the two lakes and the tunnel

moments.what: the high lake fills in, blue, on the mountain top
its name writes on
the low lake fills in at the mountain's foot
its name writes on
a glowing tunnel draws itself under the mountain
rock cracks along the tunnel's path

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: On top sits one lake, Marchlyn Mawr. At its foot sits another, Llyn Peris. And tunnels run through the rock between them.

params.place: on the map: Britain at night, then the two lakes

moments.what: the map goes dark blue, a moon rises
house lights across Britain switch off
a price sign over Wales drops to low
the camera dives back to the lakes, water flows up the tunnel
arrows climb the mountain
the high lake's level rises on its gauge

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: At night, while Britain sleeps and power is cheap, the machines pump water uphill, from the low lake into the high one.

params.place: on the map: Elidir Fawr with a battery drawn round it

moments.what: a question mark bounces over the high lake
the lake ripples
a battery outline draws round the mountain
the battery's bars fill one by one
a sleeping worker in a hard hat nods by the gate
an arrow climbs from the low lake to the high one
the mountain glows
the high lake shimmers bright

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So why pump a lake uphill? Because now the whole mountain is a battery, full of water, waiting.

params.place: on the map: Britain's cities at night

moments.what: a big kettle drops onto London
a TV glows over the cities, a whistle blows
the TV screen flashes
little people stand up across the map
kettles pop on city after city
the demand needle on a sign swings to red
the big kettle wobbles on London
the TV flips to FULL TIME
the little people wave their arms

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And what it waits for is a kettle. When a big final ends on TV, millions of people get up and switch one on, all at once.

params.place: on the map: the tunnel from the high lake to the low

moments.what: gates at the high lake swing open
water pours into the tunnel
the water rushes down the tunnel to the cavern
the turbines glow
they spin fast, sparks fly
power lines race out across Wales, the figure on a pylon sign
the gates rattle
the mountain shudders as the water rushes through
a burst of light from the hall

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And then? The gates open. The water falls through the mountain, the machines spin, and out come 1,800 megawatts.

params.place: on the map: Marchlyn Mawr draining

moments.what: the high lake's shoreline shrinks
a clock sign on the dam starts turning
the hours count up on the clock
the camera rises over the top lake
mud shows at the bottom, a boat sits on it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It keeps that going for 6 hours, until the top lake is nearly empty.

params.place: on the map: Snowdonia National Park

moments.what: a ribbon is cut by the hall, the year on a plaque that stays
grass closes over the hall, which stays below as a dashed outline
the park boundary draws round Snowdonia
its name stamps on
a hiker walks over the mountain, trees and goats pop up
the hall's machines glow once more
the mountain's peak shines in the sun

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It opened in 1984, built inside the rock, so the national park above still looks wild.

params.place: on the map: Britain from above, lights racing on

moments.what: a stopwatch drops on Wales
its hand starts to sweep
the turbines glow under the mountain
power races out along lines to every city
the stopwatch stops on the figure
a kettle on London sits cold
its steam only now begins to rise

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But its real secret is speed: with its machines already spinning, it reaches full power in about 16 seconds, long before a single kettle boils.

params.place: on the map: Britain, then back to space

moments.what: a kettle pin glows on London
a mountain pin glows on Wales
a question mark bounces between them
a comment bubble pops up
the kettle steams
the camera pulls back to the globe: the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Kettle or mountain: which one surprised you more? Tell me in the comments. And next time you boil one, think of that mountain in Wales.

disclaimer: Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
